newsitem.title: INDIA: Weizman positive on Middle East peace.
newsitem.headline: Weizman positive on Middle East peace.

text.p: Visiting Israeli President Ezer Weizman said on Monday there were no easy solutions in talks with Palestinian negotiators over the elusive Hebron deal, but said he was hopeful about progress.

"It's not an easy problem. It's a difficult solution. But I am sure (there would be progress) in the very near future, I don't want to quote dates," Weizman told reporters at the start of his first visit to India.
Indian Foreign Minister Inder Gujral told reporters that the issue was discussed by Israeli and Indian delegations headed by Weizman and Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda.
"Their response was positive. They said they are trying to restore the health of the agreements, the peace process," Gujral said.
He said India had also asked Weizman to help improve Israel's ties with Syria.
"We are equally keen that their relationship with the neighbouring countries, including Syria, should improve," Gujral said.
Weizman, speaking after a colourful reception at the Presidential Palace, said he had spoken to Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai on Monday morning to discuss the Hebron issue.
"The defence ministry is doing its best," he said.
Mordechai held a 90-minute meeting with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat in the self-ruled Gaza Strip on Sunday when they discussed the standoff over the West Bank town of Hebron.
"We hope that by tomorrow evening we'll find solutions to the subjects that remain in dispute," Mordechai told reporters after his meeting with Arafat.

Mordechai said Israeli negotiators would settle the last disputes over the Hebron deal so that by Monday evening Arafat and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu could set a time to sign the accord.

The pact would give Palestinians control of 80 percent of Hebron. Weizman earlier told India's state-run Doordarshan television he did not see chances of an Arab-Israeli war over the latest crisis in the Middle East peace process.
He said Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak was planning to settle several million Egyptians in the Sinai peninsula, neighbouring Israel.

"That is not the thinking of a leader who is preparing for war," Weizman said in the interview shown on Saturday. He described Syrian President Hafez Assad as "sulking" with Israel but said that was not a hindrance to eventual talks with him.
